description: Public, append-only, real-time log of every allocation call. Owned infrastructure.
tracked_config: Vero Compass v1.6 (12-asset pool including gold, up to 6 held, inverse-volatility sizing, BTC-trend crash filter − crypto moves to cash while the gold hedge is exempt and may stay held; the hedge is funded by selling the WEAKEST-ranked holdings rather than proportionally from all of them). Tracked from 2026-08-28; entries #1 and #2 were produced by v1.3/v1.4 − see engine_changes.

honesty.live_vs_backtest: This log is the LIVE forward record from inception. Backtest is separately verifiable on the TradingView indicator.
honesty.pool: The coin pool is a disclosed input, not a claimed edge. Curated-pool backtests are survivorship-biased and are never a performance headline. The forward log is the proof.
honesty.append_only: Never back-dated, never edited. A wrong call stays.

calls.effective_since_note: Verifiable on the indicator backtest; not a live-tracked claim. Live forward record starts at inception.
calls.reason: BTC below its 120-day trend filter — system holds no crypto, sits in cash.
Bitcoin is still below its long-term trend, so no crypto qualifies. Gold has now passed its own trend gate, so the book moves out of cash and into the gold hedge.

result_period.method: daily opens, net of 0.1%/side fee + per-coin spread

detail.note: cash earns nothing and costs nothing

engine_changes.what_changed: When the book moves into the gold hedge, the money now comes from selling the weakest-ranked holdings instead of trimming every holding proportionally. Selection, pool, position count, sizing and the crash filter are unchanged.
engine_changes.why: On a survivorship-free test universe − one that keeps the coins which later went to zero − the change returns about 29% more with roughly 15 points less drawdown. That universe is the one that resembles live trading, because nobody knows in advance which coins survive.
engine_changes.what_it_does_not_improve: Measured instead on our curated 12-coin pool, the same change roughly HALVES the return and, across the full 2017-start window, improves drawdown by 0.1 points − that is, not at all. The reason is structural: those 12 coins are survivors, so the 'weakest holding' being sold is always a future winner and the rule only shows its cost. We consider the survivorship-free result the honest one, and we are publishing the unflattering one beside it rather than choosing whichever flatters.
engine_changes.known_cost: The benefit is concentrated in falling and choppy markets. Split by era, the new rule returned about 34% of the old one through the bull-dominated 2017-2021 stretch and about 141% through 2022-2026. If a strong alt season arrives, expect this version to lag the one it replaced. That is the trade being made deliberately, not an unexpected outcome.
engine_changes.drawdown_claim_scope: Lower drawdown is true from 2018 onward and strongly true after 2021. It is NOT true across the full 2017-start record on the curated pool. Any drawdown claim must name its period.
engine_changes.applies_to: Entries #1 and #2 were produced by v1.3/v1.4 and are unchanged. Entry #3 onward is produced by v1.6.
